chunks: The Shaykh, may God have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The salat during travel is two rak'ahs; there is nothing before them nor after them, except Maghrib which is three.

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel/journey (safar) — the legal condition that activates the qasr ruling and the suspension of nafilah prayers
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat — the obligatory ritual prayer; here referring specifically to the shortened travel prayer (salat al-qasr)
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: Maghrib — the sunset prayer; uniquely exempted from shortening, remaining three rak'ahs even during travel
key_terms.رَكْعَتَانِ: two rak'ahs — the shortened form prescribed for four-rak'ah prayers during travel

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the number of rak'ahs and nafilah prayers during travel (salat al-qasr) according to Imam al-Sadiq in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a chain ending at Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), establishes the Shia jurisprudential ruling of salat al-qasr: the four-rak'ah obligatory prayers (Zuhr, Asr, Isha) are shortened to two rak'ahs during travel, and their associated nafilah (supererogatory) prayers before and after are entirely suspended. The Maghrib prayer is explicitly exempted from shortening, retaining its three rak'ahs, as three constitutes its irreducible minimum.
